_live_enabled_note: Structural safety lock. While false, NO --live run can tag real contacts even with --i-have-shift-signoff. Flip to true only after SHIFT clears consent + the Mailchimp Journey + copy.
_env_note: Path (relative to SHIFT_Automation, or absolute) to the file holding this client's MAILCHIMP_API_KEY / MAILCHIMP_SERVER / MAILCHIMP_AUDIENCE_ID. Each client has their own Mailchimp account, so each gets their own env file.

test_contacts._base_email_note: Changed 2026-06-17 from +shifttest to +sittest2: the +shifttest_* dummies were permanently deleted in Mailchimp and CANNOT be re-imported (permanent delete is irreversible), so reusing them fails. Going forward, remove test dummies with the tool's `cleanup` (which ARCHIVES, reversible) instead of a permanent delete. If a base ever gets burned again, just bump this to a new +alias.

_test_contacts_note: S5 --test mode safety. In --test the tool NEVER tags a real climber. It remaps the computed queue onto plus-addressed dummies derived from base_email (e.g. lvvargo33+shifttest_survey_request@gmail.com), one per distinct tag, capped at max. All mail still delivers to base_email's inbox so Luke sees the tag land. testmode.assert_all_dummy() fail-closes the whole run if any target is not a plus-variant of base_email, so a real address can never slip through. base_email MUST contain a '+' so plus-addressing works; change it to whichever inbox Luke wants the test mail in.
_daypass_code_note: SHIFT's REAL 2nd-visit promo code (SECONDVISIT = 50% off), provided by SHIFT 2026-06-17, replacing the old SHIFT50 placeholder. Substituted into reengage_offer_v1.md as {daypass_code}. SIMPLEST path (code-only, no Beta wiring): staff recognize this one shared code at the desk and apply 50% off manually at checkout; tracking = staff tally or count of emails sent. BETA-TRACKED option (if SHIFT wants automatic redemption counts): SHIFT creates a real discount code / '50% Day Pass' product in Beta so redemptions are logged natively; then this value = that Beta code. A shared code can be re-shared publicly; acceptable for a pilot. Per-person unique codes would need a code-generation + mapping build (deferred).
_links_note: Link/CTA tokens substituted into templates by templates.render (any {token} matching a key here is replaced; unknown tokens are left as-is). survey_link = the public Google Form (Form -> Send -> link). membership_lite_link = SHIFT's membership purchase page (Membership Lite is one option in the cart there; no direct deep link exists). contact_email = the staff inbox used for the 2-week-trial and discounted-day-pass CTAs, which are staff-judged per climber so they are a 'reply / email us' ask, not a self-serve link (2026-06-04 decision). Update here, not in the .md files.
_data_note: Paths relative to SHIFT_Automation (or absolute). Where this client's Beta exports land each cycle.
_trial_skus_note: Lowercased substrings; a SUCCEEDED transaction whose items contain any of these counts as a trial purchase (the trial_purchase anchor).
_low_commitment_skus_note: Entry-level products. low_commitment minus trial_skus = the day-pass set used by daypass_repeat. Grounded in SHIFT's real Transactions export (1 day pass - adult, new day pass, 10 punch pass - adult, etc.).
_conversion_skus_note: Substrings that mean 'became a member'. 'recurring' catches monthly recurring / presale monthly recurring / 3x recurring monthly membership / unlimited monthly recurring membership; 'prepaid' catches one month prepaid. NOTE we deliberately do NOT use bare 'membership' because 'two-week trial - trial membership' contains it. converted = bought a conversion_sku OR appears in Memberships.csv.
converted_when: buys any conversion_sku OR appears in Memberships
_daypass_repeat_note: A 'day-pass regular' = bought >= min_count day passes within window_days. Feeds the daypass_to_trial nudge (requires.daypass_repeat).

reporting._note: Definitions for the REPORTING layer only (Dashboard tiles, Funnel, Insights). Mirrors the SHIFT FTV analysis workbook (SHIFT_Analysis/scripts/01_data_prep.py) so the dashboard's numbers match the analysis. These do NOT affect the Recovery Queue eligibility engine, which keeps its own trial/conversion_skus logic above. Everything here is tunable without code.
reporting._post_opening_date_note: SHIFT opened to the public ~this date; earlier first-visits are PRESALE founders. The dashboard's 'All-time' view starts here, so the headline FTV count + conversion rate match the workbook's post-opening cohort (~3,501 FTVs / ~8.1%), not the raw 3,558.
reporting._staff_note: Excluded from the FTV cohort. staff_emails is the explicit founder/staff list; any Memberships row whose prices or metadata contains a staff_tier_keyword also marks that email as staff.
reporting._ftv_qualifying_note: A climber's FTV = their earliest SUCCEEDED transaction whose product category is one of these. RETAIL/FEE/GIFT_CARD purchases do not count as a first visit.
reporting._exclude_from_cohort_note: Entry categories dropped from the REPORTING cohort entirely (dashboard tiles / funnel / insights). MEMBERSHIP = direct memberships: climbers who bought a membership on their first visit. They are already members on arrival, so a first-visit follow-up never influenced them; including them would inflate the conversion rate the tool can claim. The workbook keeps both views for the full picture; the live tool reports only the follow-up-addressable group. Does NOT affect the Recovery Queue (it skips members regardless).
reporting._product_rules_note: Ordered, first-match-wins substring rules on each line-item product name (lowercased). 'any' = match if any substring present; 'all' = match only if every substring present. Ported verbatim from the workbook's categorize_product(). Edit only if SHIFT's product catalog changes.
reporting._conversion_note: Reporting conversion = the climber has a Memberships.csv row with a real (non-empty) price/tier. Matches the workbook's converted_to_member (membership_created not null, Freeze-Fee/blank rows dropped). This is the rate shown on the dashboard tiles + funnel. (The queue's separate 'is_converted' = recurring/prepaid SKU OR any Memberships row, used only to stop messaging a member.)

survey._enabled_note: FALSE until the real Google Form + response Sheet exist (see SURVEY_SETUP.md). While false the tool ignores survey data and behaves exactly like S1 (honest, no fake answers in the dashboard). Flip to true and set source=gsheet + gsheet_id once the form is live. TRUE as of 2026-06-01: live Google Form + response sheet wired (gsheet_id below).
survey._source_note: 'csv' reads a local response file (csv_path) for dev/testing; 'gsheet' reads the live Form responses via the gsheets bridge (gsheet_id + gsheet_range).

columns.q1_overall: How was your first visit overall?
columns.q2_intent: How likely is it that climbing could become something you do regularly?

survey._columns_note: Header text in the response sheet -> our field. Match the exact Google Form question text. Edit if the form wording changes.
survey._blocker_map_note: Q3 answer text (lowercased substring) -> the blocker value the nudge_* triggers require. 'none'/blank -> no blocker.
survey._q1_tap_note: Embed-variant survey email (2x2 test, 2026-07-28): Q1 renders as five rating buttons that hit GET /s on the live server. The server appends [timestamp, email, q1, variant tag] to the Taps tab of THIS response sheet (gsheet_id above; tap_range) and 302s into the Google Form with Q1 + Email prefilled via these entry ids (from the form's FB_PUBLIC_LOAD_DATA_). If the form is ever rebuilt, refresh both entry ids.
survey._intent_map_note: Q2 answer (lowercased substring) -> intent bucket. nudge_round_two requires intent=high.
survey._safety_keywords_note: If any appears in Q4 free text (lowercased), the climber is flagged safety -> MANUAL precedence (manager call, no automated email).

triggers.name: first_visit_reengage
triggers._ab_tags_note: Subject-line A/B test (2026-07-06). Triggers the 'FTV Reengage (subject a/b ...)' journeys; verified live same day after Luke removed the entry filters. The engine buckets each recipient deterministically (sha256 of email+trigger name) and applies the variant tag; the base tag above no longer triggers any journey and is kept for reference.
triggers.description: EMAIL 2, GENERIC (two-email follow-up, client plan 2026-06-17): the 'come back, here's 50% off' offer for one-visit, no-return climbers who did NOT complete the survey. ALL pass types (day pass / 2-wk trial / guest). Survey responders instead get a matching-feedback nudge (nudge_* / nudge_round_two) that carries the SAME code; not_surveyed here keeps the two mutually exclusive, and group 'second_visit' caps it at exactly one offer email per person even for late survey responders.
triggers._reengage_fix_note: Was paused the morning of 2026-07-06: neither reengage journey fired on any tag because both had 'filter who can enter' send conditions (the S20 trap again). Luke removed the filters same morning; fresh-contact test then proved BOTH journeys send within a minute of tagging (FTV_reengage_subject_a and _b), so this trigger went back to active.
triggers._active_note: active:true = VISIBLE in the dashboard/queue for preview. SENDING is still fully OFF: the cloud copy forces live_enabled:false and the shift-nudge-send cron has NUDGE_LIVE_ENABLED=false, so the daily cron computes this queue and tags NOBODY. The 'active' flag never controlled sending (live_enabled does). To GO LIVE later: set first_visit_on_or_after (here AND on every other sending trigger) to the go-live date, build the Mailchimp Journey on each tag, then flip NUDGE_LIVE_ENABLED=true.
triggers._provisional_note: TWO-EMAIL FLOW locked per Luke 2026-06-17 (email thread w/ Isaac/SHIFT). EMAIL 1 = survey_request (day 1-2, all first-timers, even returners). EMAIL 2 (this 'second_visit' group, ~day 5-7) = ONE offer email carrying {daypass_code} (SECONDVISIT): survey responders get the matching-feedback variant (nudge_round_two for high intent, nudge_<blocker> for a named blocker), everyone else gets THIS generic one. ALL PASS TYPES incl. guests; the own_email_guard in engine.build_queue withholds any inbox shared by 2+ climbers (a guest under the host's email, a shared family inbox), so we never message the wrong person until SHIFT captures each guest's own email at check-in. FORWARD-ONLY at go-live: set first_visit_on_or_after to the go-live date on this + survey_request + the nudge_* triggers (empty now so the preview shows realistic volume). STILL OPEN before flip: Mailchimp opt-in/consent, Journeys per tag, final copy.

triggers.name: survey_request
triggers._ab_tags_note: Subject-line A/B test (2026-07-06). Chris repointed the survey journey to trigger on FTV_survey_subject_a (renamed 'FTV Survey (subject a, preview a)') and built a B copy on FTV_survey_subject_b. The engine buckets each recipient deterministically and applies the variant tag; send_it_survey_request no longer triggers any journey (it stopped sending 2026-07-04, which is how we found out).
triggers._tag_note: Mailchimp tag the journey listens for. Uses the send_it_ prefix because SHIFT's Mailchimp already had a pre-existing 'survey_request' tag that collided with our journey trigger (2026-06-17). Namespacing avoids that. The Mailchimp Journey 'Send It - Survey' triggers on this exact tag.
triggers.description: EMAIL 1 (two-email flow): the 4-question feedback survey, sent to EVERY first-timer 1-2 days after their first visit, ALL pass types, even if they have already come back (we still want their first-visit feedback). NOT in the 'second_visit' group, so it always goes; the day-5-7 offer (email 2) is separate.

triggers.name: comeback_soft
triggers.description: RETIRED 2026-06-17 (folded into the two-email flow). Was: bought a trial, no return, ~day 5. Trial buyers who didn't return are now one-visit no-return climbers covered by the unified EMAIL 2 (first_visit_reengage generic, or a nudge_* feedback variant if they completed the survey). Kept here, active:false, so the old day-5 trial nudge can be restored if needed.

triggers.name: daypass_to_trial
triggers.description: OFF 2026-06-17 (Luke: first-time visitors only for now). Repeat day-pass buyers (not a member) -> 2-week-trial nudge. Different audience from the two-email first-visit flow. Re-enable (active:true) when SHIFT wants to add the day-pass-regular nudge.

_triggers_note: PROVISIONAL pilot catalog (FTV_PILOT_SPEC.md section 14.6). Order = precedence (first = highest priority; one message per person per run, section 14.7). survey_request + comeback_soft + daypass_to_trial compute from Beta alone today; the survey-anchored nudge_* + nudge_round_two need S2 survey data and match nobody until then. MANUAL (safety) and converted-stop are precedence rules in engine.py, not rows here. Roadmap rows (trial_convert, trial_winback, member_miss_you) are added one block at a time.
